messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure stems from the “improved auto-recognition” fallback in ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(InputStream) that was added for COMPRESS-117.

Step-by-step:

1) The test passes a short, non-archive ByteArrayInputStream (a small text string).
   - The test expects an ArchiveException with a message starting “No Archiver found”.

2) In ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(InputStream):
   - It first reads 12 bytes and checks Zip/Jar/Ar/Cpio signatures. None match for a short text.
   - It then reads 32 bytes and checks for Dump. That also doesn’t match.
   - Next it reads 512 bytes into tarheader and calls TarArchiveInputStream.matches(tarheader, signatureLength).
     • TarArchiveInputStream.matches requires the tar magic/version fields at offsets around 257. For short inputs, signatureLength is far smaller than that, so matches returns false. This is correct.

3) The problematic fallback (for COMPRESS-117) then runs:
   - It constructs a TarArchiveInputStream over new ByteArrayInputStream(tarheader) and calls tais.getNextEntry().
   - If no exception is thrown, it returns a new TarArchiveInputStream wrapping the original input, assuming it is a tar.

4) Why this wrongly recognizes short text as tar:
   - The tarheader buffer is always 512 bytes; for a short text input, only the first N bytes are from the text, the rest are zeros.
   - TarArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() attempts to read a tar header via getRecord(), which uses TarBuffer. With only the buffered 512 bytes (and TarBuffer typically expecting a full block structure), getRecord may conclude EOF and return null without throwing an exception.
   - As a result, tais.getNextEntry() returns null rather than throwing. The fallback code interprets “no exception” as “valid tar” and returns a TarArchiveInputStream for the original input stream.
   - In other words, the heuristic treats “no exception” (even when no entry is found) as a positive detection, which is too permissive. For short text inputs, the zero-padded 512-byte buffer makes getNextEntry() cleanly return null (EOF) instead of failing, causing false positives.

5) This directly contradicts the test’s expectation that a non-archive should cause an ArchiveException with “No Archiver found…”.

Conclusion: The root cause is the overly permissive COMPRESS-117 fallback in ArchiveStreamFactory that returns a TarArchiveInputStream if calling getNextEntry() on a TarArchiveInputStream created from the first 512 bytes doesn’t throw an exception—without requiring that an actual entry be found. This incorrectly classifies short text files as tar archives. The detection should require a definite positive signal (e.g., getNextEntry() returns a non-null entry and/or header validation succeeds) rather than the mere absence of an exception.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
